paper_metadata.title: New insight on the influence of Re on the microstructure and creep properties of low-density Ni3Al-based single crystal superalloys

The master alloy was synthesized using a vacuum induction furnace.

Subsequently, the single crystal rods, measuring 25 mm in length and 16 mm in diameter, were fabricated through directional solidification. Using the Bridgman directional solidification method, the pouring temperature was controlled between 1560 and 1580 °C, the temperature gradient was maintained at approximately 30 °C, and the withdrawal rate was set at 3.5 mm/min.

For the 0Re and 1.5Re alloy, the solution heat treatment schedule was: 1280 °C/3 h/air cooling and 1300 °C/3 h/air cooling, respectively, followed by 1100 °C/1 h/air cooling + 850 °C/15 h/air cooling.

The results demonstrate that the addition of Re not only induces solid solution strengthening but also significantly enhances precipitation strengthening efficacy through modulation of γ′ phase size and distribution.

Furthermore, Re optimized the structure and composition of the dislocation network, forming a denser and more regular interfacial dislocation network with Re segregation, which can effectively hinder dislocations cutting the γ′ phase and further improve the creep performance.

The results demonstrate that the addition of Re not only induces solid solution strengthening but also significantly enhances precipitation strengthening efficacy through modulation of γ′ phase size and distribution.
The latter’s enhancement in Ni3Al-based superalloys is significantly higher than its strengthening effect on Ni-based superalloys and is the dominant and unique role in improving the creep life.

conflicts.description: This study finds solid solution strengthening dominant over cross-slip pinning in γ′, whereas Chen et al. reported the opposite for Ti additions.

evidence.quote: Chen et al. reported that the hardening effect induced by cross-slip in the γ′ phase is more pronounced than the solution strengthening effect in the γ phase with Ti additions [11]. This finding contrasts with the results of the present study.
